review: 1:1–1:4 the Arabic is a chain of 'what You want' (مَاذَا تُرِيد … حَيْثُ تُرِيد … مَا تُرِيد); the Hebrew keeps the root רצה in three of the four lines, since the repetition is the stanza's device, not an accident of rhyme.

3:4 רְצוֹנְךָ הוּא מַשְׂכִּי — the Arabic بُغْيَتِي نَيْلُ رِضَاك is 'winning Your pleasure is my aim'; מַשְׂכִּי is formed as the object of שִׂכָּה ('to look for', Ps 11:4), keeping the sense of a thing aimed at without the Modern Hebrew מַטָּרָה.

2:2 עַל־הֲדֹם רַגְלֶיךָ — the Arabic عِنْدَ مَوْطِئِ قَدَمَيْكَ is 'at the footstool of Your feet'; הֲדֹם is the biblical noun of Ps 99:5 and Isa 66:1, and the construct is kept as a place rather than a posture.
2:4 מִמְּךָ וְאֵלֶיךָ — the Arabic فَهيَ مِنْكَ وَإِلَيْك is 'it is from You and to You'; the Hebrew keeps the two prepositions with no verb, so the line stays the epigram it is in Arabic.
